About a third of the tickets for "GIANT BUCKS" are sold. The top prize count has held, with three of four still unclaimed. The number of tickets printed is fixed, so that is a plain good sign.

1638.headline: Top prizes are still unclaimed

1639.body:
"JUMBO BUCKS" offers a top prize of $2 million and twelve prize levels in all. The prize money leans toward many smaller prizes. Games shaped like this pay small prizes often and large prizes rarely. This design never changes, while every other number on this page does.

Everything above about "JUMBO BUCKS" comes from the Florida Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
1639.headline: How prizes are split

1640.body:
Of all the tickets printed for "MEGA BUCKS", about two-thirds are still unsold. The game is in the middle of its run, with two of four top prizes unclaimed. In every scratcher, either the tickets or the prizes run out first. The rest of this page shows the details.

The second-biggest prize left on "MEGA BUCKS" is $100,000, with six of them remaining.

The numbers for "MEGA BUCKS" will change a little by tomorrow, and this page will change with them.

1641.body:
One of POWER 20X's top prizes was claimed three days ago. A player in Florida won $1 million. The game started with four top prizes and now has one top prize. Nothing bigger can change on a scratcher.

Every line of POWER 20X's prize table below shows today's count, not last month's.
1641.headline: Another top prize was claimed

1642.body:
The prize money on "$500,000 CASH BLITZ" leans toward many smaller prizes. It is spread over six prize levels, from wins equal to the ticket price up to $500,000. Games built like this pay small prizes often and large prizes rarely. That design never changes, and it is the part you choose.

If you play "$500,000 CASH BLITZ" often, bookmark this page. The write-up is updated with each morning's data.

Today's free summary of "$15,000,000 PLATINUM PAYOUT" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.

One of HOLIDAY BONUS 10X's top prizes was claimed in this morning's update. A player in Florida won $10,000. The game started with twelve top prizes and now has eleven top prizes. Nothing bigger can change on a scratcher.

Everything here about "HOLIDAY BONUS 10X" comes from official Florida lottery numbers, current through October 28.
1648.headline: The top prize list got shorter

1649.body:
"HOLIDAY BONUS 20X" just went on sale in Florida. The game has ten full prize levels with ten top prizes of $50,000. Every scratcher starts this way and loses prizes as it sells. You are seeing this one before that starts, when it is easiest to judge.

If "HOLIDAY BONUS 20X" is your usual pick, check this page often. The prize counts change even when the ticket looks the same.
1649.headline: First day on sale

1650.body:
"HOLIDAY BONUS 50X" has joined the Florida lineup at $5 with six top prizes of $250,000. Only on the first day do the printed odds describe the game exactly, because nothing has been won. Starting tomorrow, this page shows how that changes.

Today's free summary of "HOLIDAY BONUS 50X" ends here. Every number behind it is on this page.
1650.headline: New in stores

1651.body:
"HOLIDAY BONUS 100X" just reached Florida stores with four top prizes of $500,000. A new game is the easiest kind to judge. No prizes have been claimed, and the printed odds are accurate for now. Every day of sales changes that, and this page tracks it.

How far "HOLIDAY BONUS 100X" is through its run does not decide anything by itself. It changes how closely to look at the other numbers.

Tomorrow's count on "HOLIDAY BONUS 100X" will be a little different. The game sells every day, and this page keeps track.
1651.headline: A new game is here

1652.body:
"HOLIDAY BONUS 200X" is new from the Florida Lottery. It is a $20 game with three top prizes of $1 million. Nothing big has been won yet because almost no one has played it. This page will show it when that changes.

The most common prize left on "HOLIDAY BONUS 200X" right now is $20.

Everything above about "HOLIDAY BONUS 200X" comes from the Florida Lottery's own published numbers. We only do the counting.
